A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TP-GRPO work and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The original qualitative appendix is retained as Appendix G in v2; its relocation does not indicate removed evidence.

before.justification: v1 reports original text-to-image experiments, quantitative comparisons in Table 1, training and sensitivity curves, and additional FLUX.1-dev and qualitative results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds TempFlow-GRPO comparison results, wall-clock performance measurements, and turning-point diagnostics.

M1.justification: The incremental rewards, aggregated rewards, turning-point criteria, initial-step treatment, balancing procedure, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The additional analyses do not introduce a new TP-GRPO component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate compositional generation, visual text rendering, human preference alignment, and DrawBench generalization. FLUX.1-dev experiments already appear in v1 Appendix A. The new analyses use retained task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds TempFlow-GRPO to all three task comparisons, substantially expanding evaluation beyond the original Flow-GRPO training baseline toward a competing process-reward approach. The footnote specifies a branching-only implementation that excludes TempFlow-GRPO's orthogonal enhancements; the full method is not evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 adds comparison against wall-clock training time and diagnostics at timestep t = 6 and within batches of 36 samples. Figure 4c reports curves through 4000 rather than approximately 2400 training steps, although the replacement curves are not explained. Existing model and sampling configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 6.3 adds an efficiency analysis accounting for extra sampling time. Appendix F adds targeted diagnostics comparing rewards at normal and turning points and tracking good/bad turning-point frequency during training. Existing noise-scale and sampling-window analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new batch means and turning-point counts are descriptive diagnostics, not additional uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 substantially expands the results with TempFlow-GRPO rows, wall-clock comparisons, and reward/count diagnostics, and replaces Figure 4c's PickScore trajectories. Existing Table 1 scores remain unchanged. Newly reported TempFlow-GRPO task scores are 0.9703 GenEval, 0.9693 OCR accuracy, and 24.45 PickScore; its OCR score exceeds constrained TP-GRPO's retained 0.9651 but falls below unconstrained TP-GRPO's 0.9718.

T1.justification: New Appendix C.3 introduces a gradient-based argument claiming that time-dependent advantages restore injectivity between timestep conditioning and supervision. This adds a mathematical property claim without proving it. The existing definitions and Lemmas C.1–C.3, including their proofs, are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about incremental rewards, turning-point credit assignment, efficient sign-based detection, and improved generation. New supporting comparisons do not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges additional sampling cost and argues that equal-time performance justifies it. Appendix F interprets distinct reward signals as role-specific feedback and persistent turning-point frequency as sustained supervision. Appendix C.3 adds the injectivity interpretation of reward sparsity.

D1.justification: The new Table 1 footnote documents implementation restrictions for the TempFlow-GRPO comparator, and Figure 8 adds runtime information. Appendix B's hardware, hyperparameters, reward-model links, and the pseudocode remain unchanged. Relabeling the same repository from 'Demo code' to 'Code' does not establish changed repository contents.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially broadens literature coverage to diffusion applications in image, video, 3D, and tabular generation and adds further diffusion-alignment references, while removing GRPO-Guard. New Appendix F.1 positions TP-GRPO against GFlowNet credit-assignment work, contrasting its setting with trajectory-balance constraints and explicit target densities.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 adds related-work and analysis passages, Appendix F, and acknowledgements; updates authors, affiliations, and publication information; and renumbers the qualitative appendix as G.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains comparator rows and an explanatory footnote, Figure 4c is redrawn with changed axes and curves, and Figures 8, 10, and 11 add new plots. Existing qualitative panels are retained and renumbered. These are localized additions within the established layout.

improvement.justification: The added process-reward comparator, wall-clock analysis, and turning-point diagnostics make the empirical assessment more informative and address the cost of additional sampling. The gain is limited: TempFlow-GRPO is restricted to branching, replacement Figure 4c curves are unexplained, and Appendix C.3 asserts injectivity without establishing it. Overall, the added evidence modestly improves the paper despite these qualifications.
